purpose: Classify ownership-change events and route the registration consequences without treating a transfer document or application as proof that registration has occurred.
legal_distinctions: A signed transfer instrument is not by itself proof that the register has been changed.
A contract for sale, conveyance, transfer instrument and registered title are distinct legal stages.
Inheritance and personal-representative transfers follow distinct succession and registration pathways.
A transfer can coexist with mortgages, charges, burdens, easements or other interests that require separate analysis.
Tax and registration are separate questions even when triggered by the same transaction.
evidence_requirements: transfer instrument or succession documentation where applicable
identity of parties or legal representatives where necessary
evidence of registration outcome for any claim that ownership has been registered
historical records where the transfer predates the current register state
official_routes: Tailte Éireann Land Registry registration services
Tailte Éireann forms and registration rules
guardrails: Never infer current ownership solely from a transfer document.
Never state that registration occurred without registration evidence.
Never collapse succession, conveyancing and registration into one event.
Never ignore registered charges or burdens when describing a transfer.
Never use tax treatment as proof of ownership.
